text:
morgan: Quick sync — Product & Sales want firm p95/p99 targets for the new hosted tier. I did a quick profiling pass and the tradeoffs are uglier than I expected. Can we align on what we can promise per-customer + fallback behavior?

jamie: TL;DR — microbatch size is the main knob. Larger microbatches -> much better throughput but p99 spikes (tail). p95 stays relatively stable.

ravi: Adding kernel selection changes also matters. For a few model variants the optimized attention kernel reduces mean but adds jitter on tails under contention.

alex: From Product: customers ask for single-number SLOs. Sales wants to promise p95=200ms for "standard" and p99=500ms for "premium". Is that realistic?

tess: Sales: a few large potential customers requested p99=300ms as a contractual ask. We can't just say no — need options.

sam: From SRE: tail latency correlates with KV cache misses + microbatch queues piling up. We saw spikes when cache eviction happened during concurrent long requests.

morgan: Sharing a trimmed profiling snippet I ran on staging (low-load):

```
# perf sample (staging, single GPU, seq_len=1024)
p95: 220ms
p99: 680ms
KV miss penalty: ~120ms on average (disk fetch emulation)
hot-kernel: aten_attn_opt -> 78ms
fallback-kernel: aten_attn_ref -> 180ms
microbatch=8 -> throughput 420 tpm, p99=620ms
microbatch=2 -> throughput 200 tpm, p99=310ms
```

jamie: Notes: 1) microbatch=8 increases batching efficiency but a single long request can hold the KV cache and cause eviction churn which shows up at p99. 2) Op-level kernel fallback (for certain head counts / dims) is triggered on ~6% of requests and each fallback adds ~100ms.

ravi: We tried prioritizing small latency-sensitive requests into a separate low-latency lane (microbatch=1-2) and putting bulk requests into big-batch lanes. That reduces p99 for latency tier but costs overall GPU utilization.

alex: Product follow-up Qs: 1) can we define tiers (std/premium/enterprise) with clear p95/p99 numbers and explain tradeoffs? 2) What is the expected cost multiplier to guarantee lower p99?

sam: Quick rule-of-thumb from infra: guaranteeing p99 300ms vs 500ms typically needs ~1.5-2x reserved capacity per model and more aggressive KV caching (larger memory allotment).

tess: Sales: customers will accept higher price for stronger p99 guarantees if we clearly state the uplift. Need exact numbers.

jamie: Proposal:
- Standard: p95=220ms, p99=650ms (best-effort, shared pool)
- Premium: p95<=200ms, p99<=450ms (dedicated lanes + tuned microbatch=2)
- Enterprise: p95<=180ms, p99<=300ms (dedicated capacity, larger KV cache, kernel pinning)

ravi: Implementation notes: to hit Premium we need:
- microbatch cap at 2 for low-latency lane
- kernel-selection policy: prefer optimized kernel and avoid fallbacks (requires model param guardrails)
- KV cache hit-rate > 95% (allocate more memory or warm cache on deploy)

perf-bot: Automated regression check: recent commit 9f3a2b increased p99 by ~40% on some L2 configs. See: https://perf.internal/report/9f3a2b

morgan: Action items:
- ravi + jamie: run a controlled canary for Premium lane + microbatch=2, measure p95/p99 under 2x and 4x load (due EOD Thu)
- sam: estimate infra cost uplift for Premium/Enterprise guarantees (due Mon)
- alex + tess: draft tier language and price uplift options based on infra estimate (due Mon)
- perf-bot: add a nightly regression alert for p99 delta > 10% per model

tess: Also flagging that some customers will ask for contractual p99 at model-level (e.g., search reranker) — we need per-model profiling docs.

jamie: One more detail: microbatch sizing interacts with KV cache lifetime. If we reduce microbatch we do more calls and rely more on cache hits; if cache hit-rate drops, p99 suffers. So both knobs must be tuned together.

ravi: I'll instrument per-request kernel-fallback counters and KV miss tags so we can attribute tail events to concrete causes. That should help Sales/Prod pushes during contract reviews.

alex: Sounds good. If the canary results match the proposal we'll ship tier descriptions and give Sales numbers.

morgan: OK — let's reconvene after canary. Thanks all :thumbsup:
